findings.title: Unsafe lookup of sender login can crash installation
findings.body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch compares pipeline.fetch_state('github_authenticated_user') to integration.metadata['sender']['login'] using direct subscripting. If an existing Integration lacks metadata.sender, sender is not a dict, login is absent, or metadata is None (legacy rows, webhook payloads without sender, or integrations created before this change), this raises KeyError/TypeError and returns a 500 instead of the intended error page. Use defensive lookups and return error() when the sender identity is unavailable.

findings.title: Ownership check is skipped when the Integration row does not exist
findings.body: The authenticated GitHub user is only checked when an active Integration row already exists. When Integration.DoesNotExist, dispatch returns pipeline.next_step() and build_integration will create the integration from the supplied installation_id without proving that the OAuth-authenticated user controls that installation. If a Sentry Integration record is absent because the webhook was delayed/failed or the data is legacy, a user who supplies a known installation_id could bind someone else's GitHub App installation to their organization. The flow should fail closed or verify ownership before advancing.

findings.title: Token exchange and user fetch can 500 instead of showing the failure page
findings.body: OAuthLoginView exchanges the OAuth code and fetches user info, but only parsing of the token response is wrapped in try/except. safe_urlopen and get_user_info can raise on network failures, timeouts, or non-successful GitHub responses. In those cases the request will return a 500 rather than the intended github-integration-failed error response. These calls should be guarded and return error() on failure.

findings.title: installation_id is accepted and bound even during OAuth callback
findings.body: OAuthLoginView binds installation_id from the query string on every dispatch, including OAuth callback requests, and does so before validating the state parameter. GitHub does not include installation_id in the OAuth redirect, so a crafted callback can alter the pipeline's stored installation_id, or mutate pipeline state even when state validation fails. Bind installation_id only during the initial step, after state validation, or avoid overwriting a value already bound in pipeline state.

findings.title: OAuth authorize URL is built without URL-encoding parameters
findings.body: The redirect to GitHub's authorize endpoint is built by interpolating client_id, state, and redirect_uri directly into a query string. redirect_uri contains characters such as ':' and '/' and should be percent-encoded per OAuth/form-urlencoded requirements. Use urllib.parse.urlencode to construct the URL; otherwise the request may be rejected by stricter OAuth servers/proxies, and future values with special characters could break the redirect.

findings.title: Direct-install redirect can reverse with a None installation_id
findings.body: If a request has setup_action=install and no pipeline but lacks installation_id, the code calls reverse('integration-installation', args=[provider_id, None]). Depending on the URL route converter this can generate an invalid URL or raise. Validate that installation_id is present before reversing, and otherwise redirect to a safe fallback.
